Summary: On the day after the Sabbath in Passover week, the priest waves a sheaf of the firstfruits of the harvest before the LORD, and Israel's harvest may then be eaten.
Commandment: On the morrow after the Sabbath, wave the sheaf of the firstfruits of your harvest before the LORD.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The waved sheaf gave the whole harvest to God first. Paul calls Christ the firstfruits of them that slept (1 Corinthians 15:20). Debated: some see the commanded observance fulfilled as shadow (Colossians 2:16-17); others keep feasts voluntarily as memorial, not as binding command. The site does not settle whether observance continues.
Purpose: To rehearse God's saving acts at appointed seasons (Leviticus 23); Paul calls Christ our Passover (1 Corinthians 5:7).
